response: Prompting primary care providers about increased patient risk as a result of family history does not appear to be effective in improving their ability to identify patients at high risk for common conditions. According to the available data, simple, at-the-visit family history prompts did not lead to any significant changes in primary care providers' ability to identify high-risk patients. Further studies are needed to examine physicians' perception of the utility of prompts for family history risk and to explore alternative methods for improving risk identification.
